key_insight: DocTalk improved chart-grounded medical question answering by instruction-tuning open-source language models on clinically reviewed examples.
clinical_relevance: The system could help clinicians retrieve information from discharge summaries, but improved QA scores do not establish clinical safety or patient benefit.
method: Generated 500 QA pairs from de-identified discharge summaries using sentence-level decomposition, chain-of-thought-guided question formulation, and expert review.
Evaluated six general-purpose and biomedical models before and after LoRA instruction tuning.
Tested the two top-performing models on PubMedQA for external generalization.
evidence_signal: The best tuned model achieved ROUGE-L 0.40, BERTScore-F1 0.76, and UMLS-F1 0.49; PubMedQA accuracy increased from 93.1% to 97.7% and from 93.5% to 94.3% for the two tested models.
watch_item: The 500-pair dataset and benchmark results warrant broader validation; the abstract reports no prospective clinical safety or patient-outcome evaluation.
paper_title: DocTalk: Enhancing Medical Knowledge Retrieval via Fine-tuned Large Language Models with Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for Robust Clinical Decision Support
